CLAUDE   ~/.claude.json is GENERATED, not copied — three keys, no host bytes
         hasCompletedOnboarding  skips the theme picker, whose answer could not
                    persist anyway (~/.claude/settings.json is GENERATED by
                    snug from an allowlist of the host's, and it is writable —
                    a private tmpfs copy that dies with this session)
         autoUpdates=false       the binary is a read-only bind; a self-update
                    inside can only fail
         trust      PRE-ANSWERED BY SNUG, in this sandbox only:
                    projects."/home/u/proj/sub".hasTrustDialogAccepted = true
                    so Claude Code does not ask "Quick safety check" for it.
                    One entry, for the ONE directory you named on the command
                    line; the entry is on this tmpfs and dies with the run,
                    and your host ~/.claude.json is neither read nor written.
                    What that dialog used to gate is dropped instead — see
                    the project line below (issue #460)
         not here   the host file's 62 KB: every project path on this machine,
                    org, email, account UUIDs, machine ID, MCP servers, and the
                    host's per-project tool approvals — so tools you approved on
                    the host are asked again in here
         creds      ~/.claude/.credentials.json is PROJECTED from the host's —
                    a generated file, not a copy
                    carried: accessToken expiresAt scopes subscriptionType rateLimitTier
                    NOT carried: refreshToken refreshTokenExpiresAt
                    expires:  2026-01-01T05:00:00Z (in 5h00m)
                    No refreshToken, so a stolen copy cannot be RENEWED: it is
                    bounded by the expiry above — hours — rather than by the
                    refresh token's, which is weeks. It is a timer, not a
                    kill switch: it can still outlive this sandbox
                    RENEWAL is not MINTING. The client ships an API-key mint
                    endpoint and whether THIS token is accepted there is
                    UNMEASURED, so snug does not claim it cannot mint.
                    NOTHING IN THIS RUN BOUNDS THAT: '@net' is selected, so a
                    process in here can reach that endpoint
                    login.claude = "host": a /login inside is completed on the HOST, which REWRITES
                    ~/.claude/.credentials.json there for the account ~/.claude.json names. Claude
                    Code in here reads /snug/claude/.credentials.json, a read-only
                    copy snug renews; ~/.claude/.credentials.json in here is the same projection,
                    unused in this mode. After such a /login one request may fail once; retry it.
         settings   ~/.claude/settings.json is GENERATED from an allowlist of
                    the host's — not bound, never read-only
                    carried: (none of the allowlisted keys were present)
         snug set   crossSessionInbound="refuse"  isolatePeerMachines=true
                    snug AUTHORS these; your host's values for them are
                    dropped like every other remote-surface key. Inbound peer
                    messages are refused, and SendMessage/SendFile to a session
                    on ANOTHER machine needs explicit approval (bypassImmune in
                    claude 2.1.246 — bypassPermissions does not lift it)
                    CLIENT-SIDE: a DEFAULT, not a boundary. The payload holds
                    the credential, controls its own argv, and this file is
                    writable — THREAT-MODEL.md 3.1
         never      hooks, apiKeyHelper, statusLine, env, mcpServers,
                    enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, permissions — each
                    names a program, selects/fetches code, or sets env; see
                    policy.ClaudeExecutingKeys for the full catalogue
         project    the target ships no .claude/settings.json,
                    settings.local.json or .mcp.json, so none is
                    projected — a NEW one the payload writes there is NOT
                    closed (issue #73)
